ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A Hall element is an important magnetic sensor used in various automatic control systems. A rectangular parallelepiped semiconductor material has a thickness of $a$, a width of $b$, and a length of $c$. A coordinate system $xyz$ is established using the three sides of the rectangular parallelepiped as axes, as shown in the figure. There are two types of charge carriers in the semiconductor: free electrons and holes, both with a charge magnitude of e. Holes can be regarded as free-moving particles with a positive charge. The number of free electrons and holes per unit volume are $n$ and $p$, respectively. When a constant current is applied along the $+x$ direction through the semiconductor material, a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic flux density of magnitude $B$ is applied along the $+y$ direction at a certain moment. Consequently, a stable electric field is quickly established in the $z$ direction, known as the Hall electric field. The magnitude of the electric field strength is E, and it is along the $-z$ direction.

1. Determine the direction of the Lorentz force on a free electron immediately after the magnetic field is applied.
2. If the current formed by the directional movement of free electrons along the $+x$ direction is $I_{n}$, determine the magnitude $F_{n z}$ of the net force, which is the resultant of the Lorentz force and the Hall electric force, acting on a single free electron in the $z$ direction due to its directional motion.
3. After the Hall electric field is established, the directional drift velocities of free electrons and holes in the $z$ direction are $v_{n z}$ and $v_{p z}$, respectively. Determine the number of free electrons and holes that move to the top surface of the semiconductor in the $z$ direction within a time interval $\Delta t$, and state the condition that the currents formed by the two types of charge carriers in the $z$ direction should satisfy.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
The free electron experiences a Lorentz force along the $+z$ direction.
$F_{n z}=e(\frac{I_{n}B}{n e a b}+E)$
$N_n = nacv_{nz} \Delta t$, $N_{p} = pacv_{p z} \Delta t$, $N_n = N_p$, the currents formed by the two types of carriers in the $z$ direction should have equal magnitudes and opposite directions.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a rectangular-parallelepiped semiconductor, and the coordinate axes are established along its three edges; the x-axis is along the length direction of the rectangular parallelepiped to the right, the length is labeled c, and the “Electric Current” arrow in the figure is also along +x; the z-axis is vertically upward, and the vertical dimension on the left is labeled b; the y-axis is along the obliquely upward direction, and the arrow of the magnetic field B is consistent with the +y direction; the thickness a is marked on the right side. Therefore the cross-sectional area perpendicular to the x direction is ab, and the upper surface area perpendicular to the z direction is ac. Then reason: The current direction is along +x, but free electrons carry negative charge, so when this electron current is formed, the directed drift velocity of the electrons is along -x. The magnetic field is along +y, so for electrons first calculate the velocity cross magnetic field: v_n × B = (-x) × (+y) = -z. The electron charge q=-e, so the direction of the Lorentz force q(v_n × B) is opposite to -z, namely along +z. Let the magnitude of the electron drift velocity along the x direction be v_nx. The magnitude of the electron current I_n = n e (ab) v_nx, so v_nx = I_n/(n e a b). The magnitude of the magnetic force on a single electron is e v_nx B = e·I_n B/(n e a b). The Hall electric field is along -z; electrons carry negative charge, so the electric-field force direction is along +z, with magnitude eE. The two add in the same direction in the z direction, so F_nz = e(I_n B/(n e a b)+E). After the Hall electric field is established, the number of particles reaching the top surface along the z direction equals “carrier number density × top surface area × drift displacement along the z direction”. The top surface area is ac, and within time Δt the lengths swept by electrons and holes along the z direction are respectively v_nz Δt and v_pz Δt, therefore N_n = n a c v_nz Δt, N_p = p a c v_pz Δt. In the steady state, there cannot be a net current in the z direction, so the z-direction currents formed by the two types of carriers should be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction; equivalently, the numbers of electrons and holes reaching the top surface satisfy N_n = N_p.
